Cursors

Source: R/cursor.R
cursor.Rd

A cursor is a stable reference to a place in a text or list. A plain position goes stale as soon as someone edits earlier in the sequence; a cursor is anchored to a character or element, so it keeps pointing at the same place as the contents change on any replica.

  • text_cursor() creates a cursor at the character currently at pos; pos = text_length(text) + 1 anchors it to the end of the text.

  • list_cursor() does the same for the element at pos of a list or movable list.

  • cursor_pos() returns the cursor's current 1-based position in doc. If the anchor character has been deleted, this is the position where it used to be.

One limitation applies to movable lists: a cursor on an element cannot be resolved after that element itself is moved with list_move(), and cursor_pos() then raises an error. Moving other elements, or replacing the element with list_set(), is fine.

A cursor is a raw vector, so it can be stored or sent to another replica and resolved there, provided that replica has the edit that created the anchor character.

Usage

text_cursor(text, pos, side = c("middle", "left", "right"))

list_cursor(list, pos, side = c("middle", "left", "right"))

cursor_pos(doc, cursor)

Arguments

text

A text handle, from doc_text() or a parent container.

pos

A 1-based character or element position.

side

Which side of the anchor the cursor sticks to when the anchor character is deleted: "middle" (the default), "left", or "right".

list

A list handle, from doc_list(), doc_movable_list(), or a parent container.

doc

A loro_doc holding the container the cursor refers to.

cursor

A raw vector from text_cursor() or list_cursor().

Value

text_cursor() and list_cursor() return a raw vector and cursor_pos() an integer.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
text = doc_text(doc)
text_insert(text, 1, "world")

cursor = text_cursor(text, 1)
text_insert(text, 1, "Hello ")
cursor_pos(doc, cursor)
#> [1] 7
